name: Crucible Industries Battle Rifle BR-11 'Tribunal'
description:
The BR-11 Tribunal is a 7.62mm battle rifle built for Crucible's corporate adjudication teams — security forces authorized to enforce contract disputes through direct action. The weapon's onboard system maintains a legal log that timestamps each engagement with the relevant contract clause being enforced, creating a chain of evidence that satisfies corporate arbitration courts. Every trigger pull is a legally documented act.

Mechanically, the Tribunal is a refined version of the FR-9 Ironmonger refit with precision components. The barrel is chrome-lined match-grade, the trigger is a two-stage unit adjustable from 1.5 to 3.5 kilograms, and the action is glass-bedded into the receiver for consistent accuracy. BCI integration provides legal overlay information — the operator sees contract boundaries, authorized engagement zones, and target authorization status in real-time.

Crucible designed the Tribunal to make violence bureaucratic. Every aspect of the weapon exists to ensure that when force is applied, it is documented, justified, and legally defensible. This makes the BR-11 the most civilized instrument of brutality in production.
specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm caseless
effective_range: 650m
rate_of_fire: 600 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 20 rounds
weight: 4.3 kg
tactical_use: The Tribunal functions as both weapon and legal instrument. Its precision components deliver match-grade accuracy for engagements where clean, documented kills are required — a stray round into non-contracted areas creates legal liability. Operators are trained to fire only within authorized engagement zones, and the BCI overlay ensures they know exactly where those boundaries lie. The legal logging system has a secondary tactical benefit: it discourages unauthorized use, since every round is audited.
cultural_context: The Tribunal represents the intersection of violence and bureaucracy that defines corporate sovereignty. In a world where contracts carry the force of law and enforcement is privatized, the BR-11 is the physical manifestation of corporate justice. Being targeted by a Tribunal operator means your death will be filed, reviewed, and archived. The weapon's nickname 'Judge Gun' captures its role perfectly — it doesn't just kill, it adjudicates.
story_hooks: A Tribunal operator discovers their legal overlay has been manipulated — the 'authorized targets' displayed in their BCI were actually civilians reclassified by a corrupt contract manager.

The legal logs from a BR-11 recovered at a crime scene prove the killing was authorized under a contract that technically doesn't exist. Someone fabricated an entire corporate dispute to justify murder.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purposeful battle rifle with an almost surgical aesthetic. The BR-11 Tribunal presents a clean, modular silhouette that emphasizes precision over brutality—angular receiver lines, a prominent top-mounted rail system, and a distinctly corporate industrial design. The weapon reads as legitimized violence: every surface serves documentation rather than decoration.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 965mm, barrel length 508mm, receiver width 85mm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced—4.3kg distributed across glass-bedded components feels substantial without being unwieldy. The precision engineering translates to a rifle that settles naturally in supported fire positions.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum receiver with chrome-lined steel barrel. Polymer furniture in reinforced nylon composite. Internal components machine-finished steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed satin accents on the receiver. Chrome barrel shows subtle wear patterns. Polymer grips feature a subtle crosshatch pattern. Overall aesthetic: industrial-corporate rather than military.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with brushed steel and black anodized accents. Minimal visual ornamentation—function-first palette.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with slight ergonomic finger grooves. Cool, slightly tacky to bare skin; designed for gloved operation. Selector lever is knurled steel.
distinctive_features: Integrated neural-link port (recessed, DIN-standard) mounted on upper receiver above trigger guard
Illuminated contract-status indicator: small LED tri-state (green/amber/red) integrated into magazine well
Precision two-stage adjustable trigger visible through cleanly machined trigger guard
Top rail system with subtle Crucible Industries branding etched discretely
Barrel shroud with micro-venting for thermal management—grid pattern visible under direct light
Serialized legal-logging component (encrypted smartchip) housed in a sealed, tamper-evident module at the gas tube junction
Charging handle knurled for gloved operation, with subtle Crucible Industries logo
Magazine well with witness holes showing round count—functional aesthetic
Muzzle brake with asymmetrical porting—refined rather than aggressive appearance
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries logo (angular Φ symbol integrated with corporate sigil) on left side of receiver, forward of trigger guard. 'BR-11 TRIBUNAL' designation stamped on barrel, above gas tube. Rho-Series Production Facility mark on right side of receiver. Serial number and legal certification stamps on receiver bottom, covered by a removable access panel.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained and clean. Corporate adjudication forces keep weapons in pristine condition for legal admissibility. Minor powder residue in action components after field use, but no battle scarring. Wear patterns are minimal—this is a weapon that sees carefully authorized use, not sustained combat.
